  "text": "The elevator in my new building had a button marked HOME beneath the basement button.

I assumed it was a joke.

On Thursday, carrying groceries and half asleep, I pressed it instead of six.

The elevator descended.

After a while, the floor numbers went dark.

When the doors opened, I was looking into the kitchen of the house where I grew up.

Not a similar kitchen. Ours. The chipped yellow counter. The calendar permanently turned to April. My father's reading glasses beside the sink.

He had been missing for nineteen years.

A kettle began to whistle.

“Could you get that?” he called from the next room.

I kept one foot inside the elevator and reached for the stove.

The kettle stopped before I touched it.

My father appeared in the doorway, exactly as I remembered him, except for his hands. They were very old.

“Don't put your bags down,” he said.

Behind me, the elevator chimed.

He looked past my shoulder.

“And don't let her help you.”

A hand reached from inside the elevator and gently took one grocery bag.

I turned.

My mother stood beside the buttons, smiling. I had spoken to her that morning. She was in Florida.

“You found him,” she said.

My father backed into the next room.

The bag split. Oranges rolled across the kitchen floor.

My mother watched them settle.

“Now,” she said, “we'll have to stay until you've picked those up.”

My father began to cry.

Under the table lay hundreds of oranges, collapsed and black with age.

He knelt among them and reached for another."
